sentences.text:
ORAL ORDER 1. RULE. Learned APP waives service of rule for the respondent-State.
2.

The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R.NO.11203038230219 of 2023 registered with Mangrol Police Station, Junagadh for offence under Sections 376(2)n, 323, 506 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5(L), 6, 8 and 12 of the POCSO Act.
3. Learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

4. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18670/2023 ORDER DATED:

sentences.text: I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.
In present case, the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
As per the story narrated in the FIR, the present applicant and the prosecturix were working together.
The present applicant had called the prosecutrix at his place under the guise of some meeting.

The prosecutrix had gone to the place of applicant where the applicant had physically abused her, and thereafter,
had threatened of dire consequences, if the prosecutrix informs anybody about the incident.
Again on the next day, the present applicant had called the prosecutrix and the prosecturix had gone to the place of applicant.
Thereafter again, the prosecutrix was threatened, and thereafter, she was asked to send the photographs of her mother in compromising condition.
The said story narrated by the prosecturix in the FIR does not inspire any confidence.

6. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40.
7.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present application is allowed.

Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
11. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
12. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
